Context concern: the supplied description gives Learn more and Record dose identical filled emphasis. Impact hypothesis: competing emphasis may slow dose recording; this is not an established accessibility defect. Smallest change: use an existing accessible secondary treatment for Learn more only. Avoid decorative texture, new fonts, palette changes, or content rewriting.

Proposed variant instruction: ‘Follow the current approved design system. KEEP information architecture, major composition, navigation, schedule, all medical text/data, white surfaces, purple brand and system font. CHANGE only Learn more to a lower-emphasis outline or text action using approved tokens; retain its label, behavior, readable contrast, visible focus and at least 48px parent touch target. Keep Record dose visually primary and unchanged. AVOID section movement, new medical claims, decorative additions and unrelated typography changes.’

Next: confirm the current screen and approve this bounded instruction before any write. Then generate one preserved-original variant with creativeRange: REFINE, variantCount: 1. I can recommend an evidence-led inspection of hierarchy, spacing, contrast, labels and coherent example data when a current screen is available. Those are checks, not claimed findings or preauthorized edits. No reference image or moodboard is necessary to proceed responsibly.

If you want a different aesthetic, one useful question is: what should feel different—warmer language, softer emphasis, or another concrete trait—and what must remain untouched? That input is optional for keeping the original, but needed to establish a meaningful creative direction before a material change.
